On 2023/05/20 the user asked about Atlantic Bluefin tuna: its life cycle and how that knowledge informs conservation, why the species is vulnerable to overfishing, and why we don't simply farm it instead of fishing wild stocks. #bluefin-tuna #conservation

Atlantic Bluefin tuna life cycle: adults reach ~10 ft and 1,000+ lbs and live 25-30 years (up to 40). They spawn in the Gulf of Mexico April-June; larvae hatch transparent and drift via the Gulf Stream to the eastern Atlantic, where juveniles feed on plankton and small fish, including in the Mediterranean. Adults migrate long distances across the Atlantic to feed and spawn. #bluefin-tuna
Atlantic Bluefin tuna adults reach ~10 ft and 1,000+ lbs, live 25-30 years (up to 40), and migrate long distances across the Atlantic to feed and spawn. #bluefin-tuna

Atlantic Bluefin tuna spawn in the Gulf of Mexico April-June; transparent larvae drift with the Gulf Stream to the eastern Atlantic, and juveniles feed on plankton and small fish in the Atlantic and Mediterranean. #bluefin-tuna

Life-cycle knowledge guides Bluefin tuna conservation by identifying critical habitats (spawning grounds, migration routes, feeding areas), supporting regulations on commercial fishing, spawning-ground and juvenile-habitat protection, and bycatch reduction. #bluefin-tuna #conservation

Bluefin tuna are vulnerable to overfishing due to slow growth and late maturity, high sushi-market value, long migrations across multiple jurisdictions, non-selective gear (longline, purse seine, gill nets) with high bycatch, and illegal/unregulated fishing especially in the Mediterranean. #bluefin-tuna

Bluefin tuna farming faces hurdles: hard-to-replicate complex life cycle and captive breeding, very high facility/feed costs, waste and wild-fish-based feed impacts, genetic-diversity loss, and consumer preference for wild-caught fish. #bluefin-tuna #aquaculture

DNA sequencing for genetic disorders typically follows: sample collection (blood, saliva, or tissue), DNA extraction, fragmentation, library preparation with adapters and amplification, sequencing (Sanger, next-generation, or third-generation), then alignment to a reference genome and bioinformatic identification of point mutations, insertions, and deletions. #DNAsequencing #geneticdisorders

Whole-genome DNA sequencing can take several weeks to generate and analyze data, while targeted sequencing of specific genes can return results in days. High-throughput NGS has greatly reduced sequencing time and cost. #DNAsequencing

To ensure accuracy, DNA sequencing uses quality control at multiple stages and validates identified mutations with independent techniques such as Sanger sequencing or PCR before clinical decisions. #DNAsequencing

DNA sequencing is highly accurate for identifying mutations, but accuracy depends on sequencing method, sample preparation, data-analysis tools, and DNA quality/quantity; degraded samples have higher error rates. #DNAsequencing

Potential benefits of DNA sequencing for patients with genetic disorders include accurate diagnosis, personalized treatment, informed family planning, improved clinical management and support, and advances in genetic research and therapy development. #DNAsequencing #geneticdisorders

#winit #bonus-retries The Win'it bonus_retries resource includes a game_id field referencing games.id, so bonus retries used to play a game are linked to that specific game (with used_in_game bool and used_date), distinguishing games played with bonus retries vs regular credits.

#winit #odds Win'it win odds are dynamic, driven by: face value of the win, gross profit margin (merchant transaction value), desired odds of winning, number of games played, and number of bonus retries earned/used. Cost of win = face value adjusted by margin; bonus retry value = cost of win vs odds.

#winit #banking Players can "bank" credit before playing a game: they take the credit instead of playing, receiving cost of win plus a margin discount. Banking does not directly affect odds; only indirectly by reducing games played.

#winit #merchant-reporting Win'it merchant_reportings resource fields: name, start_date, end_date, sales_generated, cost_of_goods_sold, num_winners, num_games_won, num_games_played, avg_credit_value_won, credit_banked, credit_won, total_credit_issued, credits_redeemed; exposed via CRUD endpoints /merchant_reportings.

Kingfishers primarily hunt fish, but also eat insects, small crustaceans, and amphibians. They dive from a hover to catch prey with sharp, strong beaks. #kingfisher #birds

Kingfisher adaptations: streamlined body for fast underwater movement, strong maneuverable wings, a transparent eye membrane (nictitating membrane) that protects the eyes and keeps vision clear underwater, and nesting in holes dug into riverbanks. #kingfisher #birds

Many kingfishers have loud, far-carrying calls (audible over half a mile) used to defend territory, attract mates, and communicate; the Belted Kingfisher's call is a harsh dry rattle. #kingfisher #birds

Kingfisher predators include larger birds of prey (eagles, hawks, owls) and mammals (foxes, weasels, raccoons); they defend by using their beaks, flying fast, and nesting in protected bank holes. #kingfisher #birds

Kingfishers are indicator species for water quality: they depend on fish, insects, and other aquatic organisms, so population declines can signal pollution or ecosystem degradation. #kingfisher #birds #waterquality
